newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields closed mainly unchanged on Friday after a volatile and foreign-driven session.

Dealer said the big question now was how to interpret statements made by Sweden's central bank this week that monetary policy would not necessarily follow the same pattern as in the past. Right now there is great confusion in the market.
"It will be interesting to see if the central bank chooses to comment upon it or if it will show it through its actions," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates closed flat at 4.63 percent and nine-year bond yields were also unchanged at 7.14 percent.
The nine year yield had been slightly higher and considerably lower during the day.
The crown firmed to 4.3100 against the mark compared to 4.3155 late on Thursday.

"If I would dare a guess it would be for yields to rise a touch and the crown to weaken slightly in the week to come as there are lots of profit in the books that people are eager to take," one dealer said.
News that unemployment in Sweden fell to 8.3 percent in September had little effect since the figure was in line with expectations and the market was focussed on U.S. data.
